answer: A Weekly community check-in streak over ninety days verified by witness countersignatures makes identity a record of showing up: every week the applicant signs in, the witness countersignatures go on the public record, and one missed week resets the streak to zero, so the network trusts the account that was there every week, not the one that appeared yesterday. A anchor out of place triggers the check: the claim is frozen until the streak clears. When the raven settles over the jade, the streak holds because every week carried its own proof.
